transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Lena Torres (Mariner - Head of ML), Rajiv Singh (Mariner - Infra), Maya Chen (Mariner - PM)

Summary:
Short walkthrough of Redwood Optimize recommendations focused on batching and prefix / KV cache to reduce per-token cost for Mariner Payments' transaction summarization and customer support agents. Discussed cost model, latency tradeoffs, VPC options, and next steps for a short benchmark/pilot.

Topics:
- Current workload profile and QPS (batching opportunities)
- KV / prefix caching for session-based reranking and long conversational context
- Cost model: tokens saved vs additional infra + memory for KV cache
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, VPC, encryption/KMS, SOC2

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on. I'm Sophie from Redwood, AE on your account.
[00:08] Lena: Hi Sophie, hi Daniel, thanks. I'm Lena, head of ML at Mariner. We've been prototyping chat summarization and a support agent.
[00:15] Rajiv: Rajiv here, infra. We'll be owning the pilot infra side.
[00:20] Daniel: Hey all, Daniel from the SE team. I'll take you through the Optimize walkthrough and cost model.
[00:30] Sophie: Quick agenda, we'll do a quick qual about your workload, then demo the Optimize console suggestions for batching and KV cache, run through the cost spreadsheet, and confirm pilot steps.
[00:45] Maya: sounds good. we have a constraint around 95th perc 400ms for chat latency tops in prod, anything over that is not acceptable.
[00:55] Daniel: noted. when we talk about batching, it's mostly about increasing throughput at the expense of tail latency if you let requests wait to fill a batch. there's also continuous batching which is smarter about micro-batches.
[01:20] Lena: our RPS is bursty — mostly spikes after settlements batch windows — avg 30 rps, peak 220 rps for parts of the flow. sequence lengths vary; summaries are 1.2k tokens average.
[01:40] Daniel: ok that profile is actually where KV cache can help, especially for customer threads where prefix context repeats — you can save tokens by caching key/value states for the prefix and avoid re-encoding repeated context.
[01:58] Rajiv: can you quantify savings? we care about cost but also memory footprint on the dedicated machines.
[02:06] Daniel: yes, in the spreadsheet I shared we model three levers: batching (larger batch size reduces per-token compute), prefix/KV caching (reduces tokens sent to the model), and quantization/dedicated config. for a typical conversation with 70% repeated prefix we see 30-45% token savings from KV cache alone.
[02:30] Lena: 30-45% is promising. what's the memory cost per session for the KV cache?
[02:36] Daniel: depends on model and kv-d type; ballpark for a 32k context model is ~40-60KB per active session for the KV state if you're using compressed storage and sharded cache. for 10k concurrent sessions that's a few hundred MB to couple GBs.
[02:58] Rajiv: couple GBs is ok, but we have strict network egress billing and can't add too much cross-AZ traffic. does Redwood's private deployment support local cache co-located with workers?
[03:10] Sophie: yes — with Dedicated or Private you can configure the cache nodes co-located on the same AZ/nodes. we also have routing policies so requests stay local to reduce egress.
[03:25] Maya: if we host with Redwood hosted API, does the KV cache live in Redwood infra? how long is retention?
[03:33] Daniel: hosted default is ephemeral per session and TTLs are configurable. you can choose session TTLs and prefix eviction policies. for PCI-related PII concerns, with Private you control retention and can integrate your KMS.
[03:50] Lena: security's huge for us, we need SOC2, SSO, audit logs and KMS integration.
[03:57] Sophie: we will attach SOC2 and security docs — Redwood supports SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integrations on Private. I will share the security pack after the call.
[04:10] Daniel: jumping into the Optimize console — (background clicking) — here you can see suggested batch sizes per model and per route, plus recommended kv_cache TTL and hit-rate assumptions.
[04:30] Daniel: for your summary pipeline where avg seq is 1.2k, we recommend smaller micro-batches (batch size 4-8) to keep latency under your 400ms 95th, and enable prefix caching for the 70% repeated context flows.
[04:50] Lena: can you show numbers? like per 1000 requests what's the token cost delta?
[04:55] Daniel: sure in the cost model tab — base with no batching or cache: ~160k tokens per 1k requests; with batching to 4 and KV cache at 70% hit rate it's ~95k tokens per 1k requests — roughly 40% token reduction.
[05:20] Rajiv: that matches your earlier 30-45% range. the spreadsheet also includes compute ops cost, right? GPU minutes?
[05:28] Daniel: yes it's tokens * throughput cost plus GPU runtime; batching reduces per-token GPU overhead, so the GPU minutes drop a bit too. we model dedicated monthly reserved vs hosted on-demand.
[05:40] Maya: what about latency variance? if we batch to 8 we might gain cost but blow past 400ms at p95.
[05:48] Daniel: exactly — tradeoff. Optimize recommends dynamic batching thresholds and latency SLO-aware batching: hold for X ms or until batch size N. for your SLO we recommend hold 10-20ms and max batch 4. that keeps p95 within limit.
[06:05] Lena: is that implemented in the runtime or in our client side?
[06:09] Daniel: in the Redwood serving runtime; you configure per-route policies and the router enforces them.
[06:18] (brief cross talk)
[06:30] Rajiv: about quantization — are you recommending 4-bit or 8-bit? impact on quality?
[06:38] Daniel: for many LLMs 4-bit quant gets you near identical quality for generation tasks; but for some heavy-token summarization we suggest running an eval set. Optimize can recommend quant+model combo. that's part of the pilot.
[06:55] Lena: pilot — what do you need from us to run a pilot?
[07:00] Sophie: ideally: dev cluster access or a sample traffic replay, sample prompts and expected outputs, security contact to enable VPC peering if you want Private/Dedicated, and target SLOs.
[07:12] Rajiv: we can provide a replay and a dev cluster. timeline?
[07:16] Sophie: we typically do a 2-3 week pilot: week 1 profiling + baseline, week 2 optimize config + benchmark, week 3 validate and handover.
[07:26] Maya: budget question — reserved dedicated vs hosted — what's the break-even?
[07:33] Daniel: it depends on sustained QPS. in your spreadsheet we modeled a 12-month reserved node commit and found dedicated becomes cheaper if avg sustained throughput is > 50 rps across peak windows. we'll send the scenario table.
[07:50] Lena: any other gotchas we should be aware of?
[07:52] Daniel: cold-start KV cache warmup; initial hit rates take time — Optimize suggests seeding caches with recent state during rollout. also ensure trace sampling to monitor p95.
[08:05] Rajiv: about tracing — does the Console show token-level latency and cost breakdown?
[08:11] Sophie: yes Console has per-route token-level cost, per-request latency histograms, and model-level cost breakdowns. you'll be able to filter by route, model, and time window.
[08:25] (15min mark)
[08:30] Lena: we have internal compliance that requires access logs stored for 12 months. Can Redwood export audit logs to our S3?
[08:38] Sophie: yes we have log exports to customer S3 for Private/Dedicated. Hosted can push to customer logs with integrations too.
[08:50] Maya: any concerns about PII in the KV cache?
[08:54] Daniel: best practice is to avoid storing raw PII in KV; instead store embeddings or identifiers and keep PII in your own encrypted store. for strict PCI you may want Private with KMS.
[09:10] Rajiv: network egress — if we use Redwood hosted but region mismatch egress could be big.
[09:16] Sophie: we can pin region and use routing policies to keep compute in region. for strict cost control Dedicated/Private avoids outbound egress to Redwood backbone.
[09:30] (noise)
[09:40] Daniel: demoing the cost sheet quickly: here's scenario A (hosted, no cache), B (hosted + cache), C (dedicated + cache + quant). B saves tokens and cost, C has higher fixed cost but lower per-token over time.
[09:57] Lena: could you annotate expected p95 in each scenario?
[10:00] Daniel: annotated — scenario A p95 ~350ms, B ~360-420ms depending on batch hold, C with dedicated optimized kernels ~320ms. again depends on model size and sequence distribution.
[10:20] Maya: sounds like dedicated gives better latency and predictable cost if we commit.
[10:25] Sophie: yes and with Dedicated you get autoscale and burst cap too.
[10:35] Rajiv: question on KV eviction: if we have long-lived accounts with long conversations, memory could grow. how do we tune eviction?
[10:44] Daniel: TTLs, LRU, and active session sharding — Optimize gives suggested TTLs based on observed recency. you can also limit per-account active sessions.
[10:55] Lena: do you support model rollbacks if quality regressions happen after quantization?
[10:59] Daniel: yes rollouts and automatic fallback policies are built-in; you can canary quantized models and auto-fallback to float if eval metrics degrade.
[11:10] Sophie: ok let's recap next steps — action items noted — Sophie will send the cost spreadsheet and security pack; Daniel will run benchmarks; Rajiv to provide replay; schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-03-10.
[11:25] Lena: good. also please include estimated infra footprint numbers per scenario so infra can plan.
[11:31] Sophie: will do.
[11:35] Maya: quick question — competitor comparison? we've evaluated OpenAI for hosted, Pinecone for vector store. how does Redwood differ?
[11:44] Daniel: Redwood is inference-first: focused on serving/runtime optimizations (batching, kernel selection, kv cache) and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private. Pinecone is for vector DB — complementary. OpenAI is model host; Redwood focuses on deployment control + cost/latency optimizations.
[12:00] (small closing)
[12:05] Sophie: thanks everyone for your time. I'll share the attachments and follow-up.
[12:10] Lena: thanks — looking forward to the pilot.
[12:15] (call ends)
